title: Phoenicians found Carthage
description: Added from the Generations curriculum import (Taking Africa for Jesus). Dated only by the Generations books cited below; no tier 1–4 chronology covers this event.

sorting_basis.note: Tier 2: CFAH Reply to Beckman (Griffith & White, Part 3): 869/868 BC. Sort changed by the Reply to Beckman pass (2026-11-13): was provisional 900 BC.

chronologies.citation: Griffith & White, "A Reply to Beckman’s Defense of Thiele’s Chronology, Part 3: The Founding Dates of Tyre and Carthage," OSF preprint v1.2 (2025), doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/9V65S, Table 2, row 869/868, p. 46
chronologies.note: Carthage (re)founded by Dido; confirmed by four Phoenician sources and Josephus.

chronologies.citation: Taking Africa for Jesus, ch. 7 "Cyprian of Carthage", PDF p. 64 (printed p. 64)
Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020), ch. 7 "Western and Eastern Europe After the Flood (2518 BC – AD 33)", PDF p. 238 (printed p. 237)
chronologies.edition_note: 1st ed. (2020); not in 2nd ed. (2024): no dated statement for this was found in the 2nd ed. (2024).

chronologies.date: “In the seventh year of his reign, his sister (Dido), fled from him, and founded the city of Carthage in Libya (b.c. 878)”
chronologies.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 30; Menander of Ephesus, ap. Josephus
chronologies.note: The parenthesis "(b.c. 878)" is printed in the sentence, immediately before the Josephus citation. It is not stored as year_bc_ad. Whether it is Menander's figure or the editor's gloss is open (H2). Generations, on founding-of-carthage, prints "Sometime between 800 and 900 BC" (provisional). 878, if it is a year, falls inside that range. It does not set the sort.
